newsitem.title: USA: Mass. man pleads in stolen Polaroid case.
newsitem.headline: Mass. man pleads in stolen Polaroid case.

text.p: A Saugus, Massachusetts man pled guilty to federal charges of illegally possessing stolen Polaroid Corp cameras and illegally using the company's trademarks, officials said.

Boston's U.S. Attorney Donald Stern and U.S. Customs Special Agent Walter Biondi said in a joint statement that Carl Fuccillo, 56, was charged with possession of stolen goods from an interstate or foreign shipment and trafficking in goods using counterfeit trademarks.
On July 20, 1994, officers from the Lynn Police Department seized 60,000 stolen Polaroid cameras and 65,000 counterfeit Polaroid display boxes from Fuccillo's business in Lynn, Mass, officials said.
The cameras were stolen from the Moran Cargo Terminal in Charleston, Mass. in November 1993, officials said.
Fuccillo faces a maximum penalty of ten years imprisonment on both charges and a $250,000 fine for the illegal possession charge and a $2 million fine for the trademark charge, officials said.
